# Getting Started

Figma: [Getting Started](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-876)

The starting point for Syntropy - Safqah’s design system. What this file is, what’s inside, why it exists, and how designers and engineers use it. Read this first.

## Welcome to Syntropy

Syntropy is the single source of truth for Safqah’s product interface - one governed, fully tokenised, bilingual (Arabic RTL + English LTR) system that every screen is built from. Nothing in the product is drawn from scratch; it is composed from the components and tokens defined here. This page is the map: what Safqah is, why this file exists, what’s inside, and how to use it.

## What “Safqah” means

Safqah (صَفْقَة) is Arabic for a deal - a transaction, a bargain struck and sealed with a handshake. Safqah Capital is a Saudi, Sharia-compliant fintech where people invest in real, vetted deals. The name shapes the whole system’s tone: clear, trustworthy, and built around the moment a deal is made.

## Why we built this

Before Syntropy, Safqah’s UI was spread across fragmented, inconsistent files - a legacy design system plus ad-hoc product screens, with duplicated components, raw hex colours, and mismatched Arabic/English handling. Syntropy replaces all of it with one library, built on five commitments:

- One source of truth - every button, input, card, list and badge is a published component. Screens compose from them; they are never re-drawn.
- Fully tokenised - colour, type, spacing, radius and elevation are variables. Change a token and the whole system follows. No raw values.
- Bilingual by design - every component ships LTR (English) and RTL (Arabic), properly mirrored, not merely flipped.
- Governed & auditable - naming, status and accessibility are enforced. The library is the contract between design and the Flutter codebase.
- Built atoms → molecules → organisms - bottom-up, so every piece is reusable and consistent.

## What’s in the file

The file reads top-to-bottom in the Pages panel, grouped by labelled section dividers - Foundations, Components, Governance and Internal.

### Foundations

Colours, Typography, Logos, Icons, Effects (elevation & soft shadows), Layout and Illustrations - the tokens and primitives everything else is built on.

### Components (02–08)

- 02 · Actions - Button, IconButton, Link, FAB, ButtonGroup, SocialButton.
- 03 · Form & Input - Input, OTP, Amount, Select, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Slider, FileUpload, FormField, Date/Time Picker, Search, TextArea, Combobox, NumericStepper.
- 04 · Data Display - Tag, Badge, Avatar, Tooltip, StatusPill, Stat, KeyValue, Divider, Timeline, ProgressBar, Charts.
- 05 · Feedback - Alert, Toast, Banner, EmptyState, Skeleton, Loader, Progress, Dialog, Popover.
- 06 · Navigation - AppBar, TabBar, BottomSheet, Modal, Drawer, Breadcrumb, Pagination, Stepper, BackButton, NavigationRail, ScrollContainer, SegmentedControl.
- 07 · Cards & Lists - CardDeal, CardGoal, CardAction, CardInfo, ListItem, ActionList, List, Section, Accordion, Carousel, Table, HeaderCard, NewsCard, Menu.
- 08 · Safqah-Specific - InvestmentCalculator, ReservationTimer, Payouts, PortfolioHeader, GoalTracker, DealTimeline, Sharia & CMA Disclosure, ProvinceSelector, RatingScale, TierBadge, KYCStep, brand logos, QualifiedCalculator, Guarantees, Issuance Row.

## How to use it

### For designers

- Insert components from the Assets panel - never detach or redraw them.
- Apply colour, type, spacing, radius and elevation through variables, never raw values.
- Pick the right Direction (LTR / RTL) for the locale - the mirrored layout is built in.
- Every component has a Documentation page: check it for props, states, tokens and usage do/don’ts.

### For engineers

- Components map to the Flutter component library; the same names carry across design and code.
- Tokens map to the code token layer - bind to the token, not the value.
- Each component’s Code Reference section shows the Flutter usage and prop mapping.

## Conventions

- Pages are ordered NN‹letter›. Name (e.g. 02a. Button); coloured dividers group the families.
- Components use PascalCase; variant properties use Title Case that matches what they render.
- Every colour, size and radius binds to a Primitive Core or Semantic variable - audited for zero raw values.
- Arabic renders in IBM Plex Sans Arabic; the type family is governed by a font variable so it swaps in one place.
- Elevation uses soft, single-layer shadow styles (Shadow/xs–xl on the Effects page); shadow signals depth, never state.
